name: Vantablack IR-2 'Ghost Light'
description:
A covert signal launcher that fires an infrared flare invisible to the naked eye but detectable by any IR-capable optic, BCI overlay, or surveillance system. The Ghost Light is designed for tactical signaling between operators who need to communicate position, status, or rally points without revealing themselves to observers who lack IR capability. The flare burns for 60 seconds at altitude and can encode simple messages through pulse patterns.

Vantablack developed the IR-2 for its own security operations, where maintaining covert communications during field operations required a fallback system independent of electronic networks. The Ghost Light has since become standard equipment for anyone operating in GLMZ's shadow economy — runners, smugglers, extraction teams, and criminal organizations use IR flare patterns as a communication system that is invisible to most observers and leaves no electronic trace.

The weapon's dual nature emerges from its targeting application. An IR flare fired at ground level marks a location — a vehicle, a building, a person — with an infrared beacon that is invisible to the target but visible to anyone with IR optics. Snipers use Ghost Lights to mark targets for engagement teams. Drone operators use them to designate strike coordinates. An invisible mark that only your allies can see is a death sentence the target never knows they've received.
legality: Restricted — military and licensed security operators
specifications:
caliber: 15mm infrared
capacity: 1 round
emission: Narrow-band infrared, invisible to naked eye
burn time: 60 seconds
detection range: 5 km with standard IR optics
weight: 0.3 kg
length: 180mm
tactical_use: Covert signaling, target designation, and rally point marking. Operators fire Ghost Lights to coordinate movement without radio communication, mark extraction points, or designate targets for supporting elements. The IR flare is invisible to anyone without appropriate optics, providing a significant tactical advantage over conventional signals.
cultural_context: The Ghost Light has created a parallel communication layer in GLMZ — a sky full of invisible signals that only certain eyes can see. Runners with IR-capable BCIs can read the night sky like a message board, and the flare patterns have evolved into an informal sign language. 'Reading ghosts' is runner slang for intercepting these covert signals.
story_hooks: A Ghost Light pattern has appeared above the Shelf that doesn't match any known operator's signal vocabulary — a new code, used by an unknown group, marking locations that correspond to municipal infrastructure access points. Someone is mapping entry routes into the city's core systems using invisible light.

An operator has discovered that their Ghost Light flares are being tracked — someone has deployed a network of IR sensors that logs every invisible flare fired in the district, decoding the signal patterns and mapping the covert communication network.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, minimalist signal launcher resembling a modernized flare gun with a distinctly angular, purpose-built aesthetic. The silhouette is deliberately low-profile — short barrel, streamlined receiver, no unnecessary protrusions. It reads as a tool of precision rather than raw firepower.
physical_description.dimensions: 180mm length overall, 45mm width across the receiver, 110mm height including grip. Barrel diameter approximately 18mm.
physical_description.weight_description: Exceptionally light and balanced — feels almost insubstantial in the hand despite its solid construction. Designed for one-handed operation and rapid deployment from tactical gear.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber reinforced polymer body with aerospace-grade aluminum receiver and barrel. Internal combustion chamber is titanium-alloy for thermal control.
physical_description.finish: Matte black polymer with brushed aluminum accents around the receiver. The barrel is finished in a dark anodized coating that resists thermal signature bloom. All surfaces are non-reflective to prevent visual detection.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: deep matte black (VANTABLACK proprietary coating absorbs 99.9% of visible light). Accent: brushed gunmetal gray on mechanical components and ejection port.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured thermoplastic rubber with subtle grip panels. Designed for gloved operation — slightly tacky to prevent slip even in wet conditions. No aggressive stippling; ergonomics favor control over aggressive purchase.
distinctive_features: Minimal iron sights — just a small witness mark on the barrel for basic aiming
Recessed ejection port with spring-loaded cover to prevent debris ingress
Three tiny LED indicator lights (red/amber/green) embedded beneath the safety lever for status feedback visible only to the operator
Smooth, featureless trigger guard — no aggressive geometry, designed to reduce snag risk
Ambidextrous safety mechanism with tactile detent
Serial number engraved in microscopic font on the receiver interior only — not visible during normal handling
Faint cooling vents machined into the grip to dissipate combustion heat
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VANTABLACK MOBILITY emblem (a minimalist geometric symbol) etched subtly into the left side of the receiver in matte gray. Model designation 'IR-2' stamped in microscopic characters on the barrel. No serial number visible externally.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. Minor scuff marks on the polymer body from tactical carry. Barrel shows light fouling residue from IR compound ignition. All mechanical surfaces remain clean and slightly oiled. Psychological wear: operators often keep these pristine because they represent life-or-death signaling in hostile territory.
